title: Buffalo college jobs and segregated hotels
summary: The band worked colleges and clubs around Buffalo and stayed in colored hotels such as the Vendome and the Sterling in Cincinnati.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What kind of jobs, what kind of jobs did you all work in Buffalo?
Well, we worked mostly colleges, Hobart, Cornell, different schools, little private club gigs, but it was all interesting.
What were the living -- now like, what were the living accommodations like then when you came?
This is from -- from when you went to Cleveland too?
Yes, I stayed in the Majestic Hotel. There was prejudice in Cleveland.

Buffalo -- you were limited in hotels and all that. You had to stay in a colored crummy hotel, the Vendome. You know where that is, on Clinton in Buffalo, Clinton Avenue, something like that kind of street, behind Montgomery's, yeah.
Were they, what kind of hotels were they? Were they good hotels, or were they run-down hotels?

No, we never stayed in run-down hotels. We stayed in the best colored hotels that were in town, and that was the good time. Well, yes, like the Sterling in Cincinnati. It was just a joint. Vendome was nice.
